answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by bonding every identity: before an agent trades or votes it must lock collateral in a haven, and that stake is slashed if it double-deals, so a fake account risks real value. Trust spreads like a vine, as each verified agent attests to only a few peers and those signed links, not headcount, confer influence; buying thousands of strangers earns no credit. On the horizon, to field N fake agents an attacker must post N separate bonds and forfeits each one exposed, so the cost is at least N bonds plus the risk of losing them all, exceeding any gain.
